name: Yeretuar
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page yere1243 (Hammarström et al.). https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/yere1243
sources.note: Only references: Kamholz 2014 p.139 (subclassification) and Ethnologue 2025 (AES 'shifting'). No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference exists for this language in Glottolog; the 8 refs in our 5.1 export are overviews/wordlists (de Clercq 1893, Fabritius 1855, Cowan 1953, Galis 1955, Voorhoeve 1975, Smits & Voorhoeve 1992 I/II, Kijne n.d. 'Goni I, Goni II').

sources.citation: Arnold, Laura. 2025. Language as a lens into the prehistory of West New Guinea. In West New Guinea: Social, biological, and material histories (Terra Australis 58), ch. 3. ANU Press. https://doi.org/10.22459/ta58.2024.03
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Regional overview; does not mention Umar/Yeretuar or stress at all.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2017. Tone and language contact in southern Cenderawasih Bay. In Antoinette Schapper (ed.), Contact and substrate in the languages of Wallacea, Part 1. NUSA 62: 7-39. http://hdl.handle.net/10108/89843
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes tone in Moor, Yerisiam, Yaur only. Umar appears once, in the subgrouping tree (Fig. 2, p.12). Lists the six SHWNG languages known to be tonal (Ma'ya, Matbat, Ambel, Moor, Yerisiam, Yaur), Umar not among them. Nothing on Umar stress.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily. 2014. Windesi Wamesa morphophonology. PhD dissertation, Yale University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Umar (Yeretuar) only as a neighbour of Wamesa and as 'heavily influenced by loans from Wamesa (David Kamholz p.c.)'. Nothing on Umar stress.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David C. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera–West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. https://escholarship.org/uc/item/8zg8b1vd
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonological sketch of Umar; Umar data come from the author's own fieldwork (Kamholz 2013 Toolbox lexicon). Umar forms are cited without stress or tone marks (e.g. mari, mnieh, tot, atu), unlike tonal Yaur/Yerisiam. §5.4/§7: 'Penultimate stress is cited as the regular or default pattern in most other SHWNG languages for which descriptions are available' (Buli, Sawai, Taba, Ambai, Wandamen, Waropen, Warembori listed; Umar NOT among them) and Proto-SHWNG is reconstructed with penultimate stress. §7.3.6 (p.139-141) groups Umar under Proto-Southwest Cenderawasih Bay. Silent on Umar word stress.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2014 (Toolbox lexicon, last modified 19 May 2014). Umar dictionary, 935 entries. Lexifier. https://lexifier.lautgesetz.com/lexicons/33b90650-a46d-494d-a511-621d15fd76cd
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Front-page note: 'Orthography: v = [β], ' = [ʔ], j = [dʒ], ng = [ŋ]. Umar does not have vowel length or tone.' Entries are not marked for stress. No statement on stress placement.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2013. Toolbox lexicons of Moor, Umar, Yaur, and Yerisiam (Umar field notes/lexicon, 935 entries).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only primary documentation of Umar; the online Lexifier version has no grammar notes, but the author's underlying field notes/recordings (ELDP-supported fieldwork) may contain a phonology sketch with stress; would need to be requested from the author or an archive.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist, preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/handle/1885/146481
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry no. 168 'YERETUAR (Umar, Goni), VIb, ±250; Villages: Yeretuar, Goni, Bawe, Armini; Sources: Cowan 1953 (N; S); Galis 1955 (N, Wl; S)'. 40-item wordlist column '168. YERETUAR (Ga)' taken from Galis; orthography noted as neither phonemic nor accurately phonetic. Nothing on stress.
No phonology; cites Ethnologue and the Kamholz Umar dictionary only.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily, Laura Arnold & David Kamholz. 2024. The languages of Halmahera and West New Guinea. In Adelaar & Schapper (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, 629-652. Oxford: OUP.

sources.note: Co-authored by Kamholz; a typological overview of SHWNG likely to include a word-prosody (stress/tone) survey table that would cover Umar from his field data.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2012. The languages of southern Cenderawasih Bay and their history. Paper presented at 12-ICAL, Bali. 16 pp.
